description: A cyber security incident that may have to be reported to CERT-In and the institution within six hours of detection.

fields.label: Title
fields.description: A short description of what happened, e.g. "Web shell found in an uploaded file".

fields.label: CERT-In Category
fields.options:
Targeted scanning or probing of critical networks or systems
Compromise of critical systems or information
Unauthorised access to IT systems or data
Website defacement or intrusion
Malicious code (virus, worm, trojan, bot, spyware, ransomware, cryptominer)
Attack on servers or network devices (database, mail, DNS, routers)
Identity theft, spoofing or phishing
Denial of service (DoS or DDoS)
Attack on critical infrastructure, SCADA, operational technology or wireless networks
Attack on applications (e-governance, e-commerce and similar)
Data breach
Data leak
Attack on IoT devices and associated systems
Attack on digital payment systems
Malicious mobile app
Fake mobile app
Unauthorised access to social media accounts
Attack on cloud computing systems or applications
Attack on big data, blockchain, virtual asset, robotics, 3D/4D printing or drone systems
Attack on machine-learning systems
fields.description: Type of cyber security incident as listed in Annexure I of the CERT-In directions of 28 April 2022.

fields.label: Status
fields.description: Becomes Reported automatically once both reports are recorded. Close the incident once it is contained and the follow-up is done.

fields.label: Reportable to CERT-In
fields.description: Clear only after assessing that this is not a reportable incident (for example, a false positive); explain why in the assessment notes.

fields.label: Personal Data Involved
fields.description: Students' or parents' personal data may have been exposed. The Data Protection Board and the affected persons must also be informed (DPDP Act 2023).

fields.label: Ops Alert
fields.description: The alert that led to this incident, if any.

fields.label: Detected On
fields.description: When the incident was first noticed. The six-hour reporting clock starts here.

fields.label: Report By
fields.description: Detected On plus six hours: CERT-In and the institution must both be informed by then.

fields.label: Reported to CERT-In On
fields.description: When the report was sent to incident@cert-in.org.in (or through the CERT-In incident reporting form).

fields.label: CERT-In Reference
fields.description: Acknowledgement or incident number received from CERT-In.

fields.label: Institution Contact Informed
fields.description: Name and designation of the ACGCET official informed, e.g. the Hostel Administrator or the Principal.

fields.label: Description
fields.description: What was observed, how it was detected, and what is known about the cause and the impact.

fields.label: Affected Systems
fields.description: Hosts, services, URLs or accounts involved.

fields.label: Actions Taken
fields.description: Containment, evidence preserved (logs, quarantined files, maldet reports) and recovery steps, with times.

fields.label: Assessment Notes
fields.description: Required when the incident is marked not reportable or closed.

name: Security Incident
